entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_CANCEL_TARGET
entry.description: Operator: stop responding to this target (it's been dealt with, or isn't interesting). Sent to all drones (target_system 0) and spread through the swarm; the target stays known as cancelled, so seeing it again doesn't draw drones back to it.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_RESPONDERS
entry.description: Operator: how many drones should respond to each target (hold a ring around it, or check it out). Sent to all drones (target_system 0) and spread through the swarm; repeated now and then so drones joining later pick it up too.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_MODE
entry.description: Operator: how the swarm works. Sent to all drones (target_system 0) and spread through the swarm; repeated now and then so drones joining later pick it up too.
entry.param: 0: autonomous (off the leash, sweeping the field in formation: the quickest search; in contact with the base only near it). 1: connected (always in contact with the base by relay chains, sweeping in rays out from it: slower).

entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_FIELD
entry.description: Operator to the launch base: the field to search, a rectangle with the base in its lower left corner. Starts a new mission on it (drones are told the field as they launch).
entry.param: Drones to launch on it (NaN: as many as the base starts a mission with).

entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_LAUNCH
entry.description: Operator to the launch base: launch this many more drones, one after another.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_REVOKE
entry.description: Operator to the launch base: this drone is no longer trusted (captured, or behaving like it). The base revokes its key for the rest of the mission (SWARM_REVOKE): the swarm stops listening to it, and the drone itself is told to come home.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_SPARES
entry.description: Operator to the launch base: keep this many spare airframes on its pads, charging, to take over from drones that come back to charge (see MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_ROTATION). Answered in SWARM_BASE_STATUS.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_ROTATION
entry.description: Operator to the launch base: whether a charged airframe on its pads takes off in the place of each drone that comes back to charge, flying as it, so as many stay in the air as were launched. A drone the operator sends home isn't replaced.

message.name: SWARM_TARGET_SIGHTING
message.description: A firsthand or relayed observation of the search target. Relayed copies keep the original observer and carry how old the observation is, so receivers can always keep the freshest observation no matter how many hops it took. Age rather than a timestamp, because drones' clocks aren't synchronized: each relay adds the time it held the observation plus an estimate of the radio hop. Also carries the target's estimated velocity, so a receiver can predict where it is by now, and W3C trace context, so the path this news takes through the swarm can be reconstructed as one distributed trace.
message.field: Swarm-wide target ID: sysid of the first drone that saw it (high byte) and that drone's own counter (low byte). Duplicate tracks of one target merge into the lowest ID.
How long ago the original observer saw the target, as of sending this message.
Target X in the local field frame, where it was observed.
Target Y in the local field frame, where it was observed.
Target velocity X, as estimated by the original observer (0 if unknown).
Target velocity Y.
MAVLink system ID of the drone that saw the target firsthand.
1 if the operator cancelled this target: drones keep track of it but don't respond to it.

Drones the original observer knows are responding to this target, itself included. Travels with the observation, so a drone too far away to hear the target's responders still learns that the target already has enough of them.
Radio hops from the original observer to the sender of this message (0 = the sender saw it firsthand).
W3C trace ID shared by every hop of this sighting's propagation. All zeros if tracing is off.
The sender's own span ID within that trace; a receiver that adopts the sighting records its span as a child of this one.

When the original observer saw the target, on its own clock. Unlike age_ms it never changes on the way, so it can be signed: receivers use it only to order one observer's observations, never against their own clocks.

The original observer's Ed25519 signature over the mission, observer_sysid, observed_ms, x, y, vx and vy (see brain/src/auth.rs), checked against the observer's SWARM_KEY_CERT. The rest is the relays' to update and isn't vouched for.

message.name: SWARM_KEY_CERT
message.description: A drone's public key, certified by the launch base for this mission. Sent along with sightings by their observer and by whoever relays them, now and then, so anyone who gets a sighting can check its signature.
message.field: The mission it's valid for.
The drone whose key this is.
Its Ed25519 public key.
The launch base's Ed25519 signature over the mission, sysid and public_key.

message.name: SWARM_SIGNED_COMMAND
message.description: A COMMAND_LONG from the operator, signed with the mission's operator key (see brain/src/auth.rs). Drones take orders in this form only: a plain COMMAND_LONG over the radio could come from anyone, a captured drone included, since the radio header isn't vouched for. Relays pass it on unchanged once they've checked it.
message.field: The mission it's for.

When the operator gave it, on the mission clock (ms since mission start). A drone takes only one newer than the last it took for the same drone, and only while fresh: a recorded order can't be played back later.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG.
As COMMAND_LONG (0: the whole swarm, for the commands that allow it).
The operator's Ed25519 signature over the mission, issued_ms, target_system, command and params.

message.name: SWARM_SIGNED_STICKS
message.description: MANUAL_CONTROL from the operator, signed like SWARM_SIGNED_COMMAND: flying a drone by hand is as much an order as any.
message.field: The mission it's for.
As SWARM_SIGNED_COMMAND. Also what orders stick input: only newer than the last counts.
As MANUAL_CONTROL.
As MANUAL_CONTROL.
As MANUAL_CONTROL.
As MANUAL_CONTROL.
As MANUAL_CONTROL.
The operator's Ed25519 signature over the mission, issued_ms, target and the axes.

message.name: SWARM_REVOKE
message.description: The launch base revokes a drone's key for the rest of the mission (MAV_CMD_SWARM_REVOKE): its sightings, statuses and beacons are no longer listened to, and the drone itself comes home. Repeated by the base every second and relayed by the swarm.
message.field: The mission it's for.
The drone revoked.
The launch base's Ed25519 signature over the mission and sysid.

message.name: SWARM_OPERATOR_KEY
message.description: Launch base to the ground station, over their wire only (never the radio): the mission's operator key, which the drones were told the public half of at launch, and the mission clock. Sent in answer to the ground station's heartbeat, so a new mission's key reaches it within a second.
message.field: The mission.
The mission clock as this is sent.
The operator's Ed25519 secret key for this mission.
The mission's radio link key (MAVLink 2 message signing): the ground station's radio frames are signed with it, and only frames signed with it are listened to.

message.name: SWARM_BASE_STATUS
message.description: Launch base to the ground station, over their wire only, with each SWARM_OPERATOR_KEY: what's on its pads, and how it's set.
message.field: Airframes on the pads, charging or charged.
Of those, charged enough to take off.
Drones down to charge with no charged airframe to take over from them yet.
Spare airframes it's been asked to keep (MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_SPARES).
1 if charged airframes take over from drones down to charge (MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_ROTATION).
1 if the drones' batteries run down (in the simulator: --battery-min).
The lowest charge of a drone in the air, 0-100 (255: not known).

message.name: SWARM_HIL_SENSOR
message.description: Simulator to brain: this tick's own-sensor reading. Each one starts one brain tick. Also tells the brain which system ID it is flying as, so the firmware needs no per-drone configuration.
message.field: Swarm clock (ms since swarm start).
GPS fix X in the local field frame (valid if gps_fix).
GPS fix Y in the local field frame.
1 if the GPS has a fix.
Own ground velocity X, from the drone's own sensors (no GPS needed).
Own ground velocity Y.
X of each target within sensor range, relative to the drone; the first target_count entries are valid.
Y of each target, relative to the drone.
Targets within sensor range this tick (at most 4).
System ID of each drone the proximity sensing picks up.
Other drones the proximity sensing picks up: X relative to this drone. The first nearby_count entries are valid.
...Y relative to this drone.
...velocity X relative to this drone.
...velocity Y relative to this drone.
How many of the nearby_* entries are valid (at most 6).
1 if the drone has proximity sensing (then nearby_* is what it sees, possibly nothing); 0 if not.
MAVLink system ID this brain flies as.
The battery's state of charge, 0 (empty) to 1 (full); NaN if the drone doesn't know it.

message.name: SWARM_HIL_COMMAND
message.description: Brain to simulator: the velocity command for the tick started by the SWARM_HIL_SENSOR with the same time_ms, plus brain state the simulator only uses for display and telemetry.
message.field: time_ms of the sensor reading this answers.
Commanded velocity X.
Commanded velocity Y.
0 = searching, 1 = investigating, 2 = converging, 3 = following an operator order.
1 if the brain holds any sighting.
1 if the brain has heard no other drone recently.
Target the brain is responding to (0 = none, just searching).
Observer whose report the brain just refuted in person (0 = none).
Where the brain thinks the drone is, X.
As in SWARM_DRONE_STATUS.nav.
1 once the brain wants the airframe to land (it's back at base after a return-to-launch); 2 if it's to charge (it went home low on charge, on its own).
Neighbors just declared lost this tick (0 = unused slot).
How long each lost neighbor had been silent.

message.name: SWARM_HIL_TRACE_EVENT
message.description: Brain to simulator: something worth a tracing span happened this tick. The brain waits for the matching SWARM_HIL_TRACE_SPAN before sending its radio traffic, so its broadcasts carry the new span as their parent.
message.field: Adopted only: age of the sighting when adopted.
1 = spotted the target firsthand, 2 = adopted a relayed sighting.
Adopted only: original observer.
Adopted only: hops from the original observer.
Adopted only: trace the sighting belongs to.
Adopted only: the relaying drone's span.

message.name: SWARM_HIL_TRACE_SPAN
message.description: Simulator to brain: the span recorded for the last SWARM_HIL_TRACE_EVENT.
message.field: Trace ID to carry in outgoing sightings.
Span ID to carry as parent_span_id.

message.name: SWARM_HIL_MISSION
message.description: Simulator to brain: everything the launch base tells a drone before it takes off. Its keys for this mission (see brain/src/auth.rs) and the mission itself: the field, where the base is, how the swarm works. Repeated every second, so a board that restarts gets it again; a different one means a new mission, and a fresh brain.
message.field: Mission number.
MAVLink system ID the drone flies as.
The drone's Ed25519 secret key.
The launch base's signature on the drone's public key (SWARM_KEY_CERT.signature).
The launch base's public key.
The mission's operator public key: orders signed with it are the ground station's (SWARM_SIGNED_COMMAND).
The mission's radio link key: every frame on the air is signed with it (MAVLink 2 message signing, see brain/src/radio.rs).
Half the field's east-west size: it spans -field_half_x..field_half_x.
Half its north-south size.
Where the launch base is, X.
Where the launch base is, Y.
0 = autonomous, 1 = connected (as MAV_CMD_SWARM_SET_MODE).
How free drones search: 0 = shared coverage map, 1 = random walk.
Drones the base launches on this mission (0 = not known): the formation's stretches go by it.

message.name: SWARM_DRONE_STATUS
message.description: One drone's state, for the operator's ground station. Each drone broadcasts its own once a second; others relay it, up to a hop limit and only if it's newer than the last one relayed, so the ground station sees the whole swarm even though its radio reaches only the drones near the base.
message.field: The drone this is about (not necessarily the sender: it may be relayed).
Increments with each status the drone issues; relays forward only statuses newer than the last one they relayed.
Radio hops so far.
How old the status is, as of sending (each relay adds its holding time).
Position X in the local field frame.
Position Y in the local field frame.
As in SWARM_HIL_COMMAND.mode.
Target it's responding to (0 = none).
Operator order it's following: 0 = none (autonomous), 1 = go to, 2 = hold, 3 = return to launch, 4 = manual control (sticks), 5 = manual control with the sticks' signal lost (hovering).
Last operator command it handled (MAV_CMD), 0 if none. The ground station's acknowledgement: COMMAND_ACK can't name its sender once relayed, a status can.
MAV_RESULT for ack_command.
Where its position comes from: 0 = GPS, 1 = neighbors it ranges (no usable GPS), 2 = dead reckoning.
How sure it is of its position (x, y above).

The highest system ID the drone knows of in the swarm (0 = not known), its own included: how many drones have been launched. Each drone passes on the highest it has heard, so the number reaches the whole swarm however many hops it is across, and every drone works out the same fronts for the sweep.
